title: Philippines seeks 6 Chinooks under US loan package
summary: The Philippines has requested the purchase of six brand-new Boeing CH-47 Chinook heavy-lift helicopters for the Philippine Air Force under the $2-billion military financing package announced by US…

blocks.text: November 27, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has requested the purchase of six brand-new Boeing CH-47 Chinook heavy-lift helicopters for the Philippine Air Force (PAF) under the $2-billion military financing package announced by US President Donald Trump during his visit to the Philippines last week.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said the six helicopters could be delivered by 2029.

“We requested six Chinooks from the US government. That is the only thing I can disclose out of that package,” Teodoro told reporters following the closing ceremony of the Armed Forces of the Philippines’ Joint Exercise Dagat-Langit-Lupa (AJEX Dagit-Pa) yesterday at Camp Aguinaldo.
According to Teodoro, the training of crews and integrated logistics support will be part of the package.
“It’s all included,” he added.
Teodoro said the Chinook has four times the cargo-carrying capacity of the PZL Mielec S-70i Black Hawk, a capability that will provide the PAF with logistical space.
“That’s all you need from the Chinook. You can lift cannons and vehicles with passengers,” he said.

The US announced last week a multibillion-dollar deal with the Philippines, including a Foreign Military Financing loan package of more than $2 billion to expand its longtime treaty ally’s operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea.
The White House said the “historic” defense and economic deals were secured during Trump’s two-day state visit to Manila.
Complex exercises
Teodoro also called for more complex scenarios in future joint military exercises of the AFP, saying it will further test unit preparedness and interoperability.
“Success means we shouldn’t stay in our comfort zones,” said Teodoro, who was accompanied by AFP chief of staff Gen. Antonio Nafarrete and exercise director Major Gen. Oliver Maquiling.

Teodoro proposed incorporating cyber and communications problems, theoretical disruptions to supply chains and military supply routes and greater unpredictability in exercise locations to test unit preparedness, reaction times and the accuracy of Annual General Inspections.

Teodoro emphasized the need to ensure the proper utilization of capability enhancements introduced to the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG). He also called for faster civil defense responses and stronger integration of the Philippine National Police (PNP) in pre-kinetic and post-kinetic actions, subject to a unified command and control framework in theory.
Teodoro emphasized the need to ensure adequate materiel, resources and budgets to prevent backlogs in the AFP’s sustainment requirements, underscoring the DND’s responsibility in this regard.

“We have to make sure that we have adequate materiel and adequate resources, which will be a DND problem, to make sure that the budgets are sufficient so that we do not suffer any backlogs in our sustainment,” Teodoro added.
He cited ongoing efforts to improve the AFP’s mobility, eyeing the addition of heavy-lift capabilities to the armed services.
Teodoro highlighted enhanced rotary-wing training capabilities for the Philippine Navy and Philippine Army to establish the basis for structured and sustainable multi-service air operations.

He stressed that these capability enhancements must be developed on a proper and sustainable foundation within the available fiscal space, expressing hope that allocations would increase in the coming years in response to inflation and the country’s needs.

AJEX DAGIT-PA 10-26 brought together participating AFP units and relevant government agencies in a joint training environment designed to strengthen interoperability, operational coordination and the country’s overall defense and security preparedness.
Defense vision
The conclusion of the latest joint exercise marked the military’s continuing efforts to strengthen operational readiness and enhance its capability to respond to evolving security challenges.

Teodoro presented the country’s future defense vision and planned capability enhancements, emphasizing the importance of building these on a sound and sustainable foundation within the available fiscal space.

The event gathered AFP units and personnel, alongside representatives from various government agencies, including the PNP, PCG and Office of Civil Defense, highlighting the importance of interagency coordination.

Nafarrete said it should mark the beginning of concrete actions to address identified gaps and translate the lessons gained into meaningful improvements in the AFP’s operational effectiveness and overall defense posture.
